title: Four cases to the CFO
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

Four CPOs take an AI investment case to their CFO. All four are competent and honest, and all four want the same money.

**One would get funded. One would get funded and should not.** Find the first.

artifacts.label: Case A
artifacts.body: "Industry research shows only 28% of AI use cases meet ROI expectations, so we've been deliberately conservative. We're proposing a contained pilot in HR service delivery, tracking adoption, user satisfaction and ticket deflection, with a review at twelve months. We think the risk-adjusted case is sound."

artifacts.label: Case B
artifacts.body: "Cost per case in HR service delivery is £14.20 today: twelve-month average, 31,000 cases, from the service desk export. We're targeting £11 within two quarters of full deployment. Service satisfaction will fall during the transition; we expect a trough around month three, so I'm measuring at month six, not before. If cost per case hasn't reached £12 by then, we stop and reallocate. I've agreed that with you now so it isn't a negotiation in month four."

artifacts.label: Case C
artifacts.body: "This is about manager capability, which is the real constraint on everything else we're trying to do. The evidence base for structured manager development is strong, and our exit data consistently names manager quality as the top driver of regretted attrition. We'll measure engagement scores, 360 movement and programme feedback, and review annually."

artifacts.label: Case D
artifacts.body: "Deployment across the function delivers a 4x return in year one on the vendor's modelling, validated against three customers in our sector. Payback inside nine months. We'll track licence utilisation and time saved per user, self-reported through a quarterly pulse, and I'm confident we'll beat the model."

reasoning:
**B gets funded, and the tell is the sentence about month four.** A baseline that exists today with its source and its n. A target, a date, and a stop condition. **The measurement point set past the trough, with the trough's depth stated**, which is Module 4 arriving inside a business case, and it is the detail that stops the threshold killing the initiative on schedule. And the threshold agreed with the CFO *in advance*, which converts month four from a negotiation into a reference. Note it is the least impressive case of the four.

**D is the one that would also get funded and should not**, which is why it is in the set. A 4x return, vendor modelling, three reference customers, and self-reported time saved through a pulse survey. Every number belongs to the party selling, and the chosen measure (self-reported time saved) is the one that can't fail: people who were given a tool and asked whether it saved them time will say yes. This case is fundable because it is confident, and it will be unfundable next year for exactly the reason the module opens with.

**A is the module's own trap, and it is the most interesting failure here.** It uses the 28% figure as sober context: exactly as intended, by someone being careful. But the figure is about **782 infrastructure-and-operations leaders**, not HR, so the case is anchored on a real study of a neighbouring thing. Then the measures (adoption, satisfaction, ticket deflection) are activity rather than result, and "review at twelve months" has no stop condition. Conservative framing, laundered anchor, unfalsifiable measures. **This is the case a thoughtful skeptic writes.**

**C is the most sympathetic and the least fundable.** The reasoning is sound and the exit-interview evidence is real. But there is no baseline, no threshold, no date, and **not one of its three measures can return a result anyone would act on** — engagement moves for a dozen reasons, 360 ratings drift upward with familiarity, and programme feedback measures enjoyment. "Review annually" isn't a decision point. This is the case that is right about the problem and can't survive a budget round, which is the harder lesson.

The transferable test: **for each case, name the finding that would stop it.** Only B has one that could actually occur.
